Week of Writing 2026: Events for Grad Students and Postdocs
Hosted by the MU Writing Center, the annual Week of Writing is a celebration of writing in all its forms. This year’s theme, Writing “Above the Table”, draws inspiration from tabletop role-playing games (TTRPGs). These collaborative games allow players to create a story together. Talking “above the table” refers to discussions held out of character, where the group sets expectations, discusses strategy, and agrees on processes and boundaries for their shared storytelling experience. To that end, W.O.W. 2026 focuses on the process of writing, including the opportunities for collaboration, the struggles, and the joy of…

Dean of the Graduate School Honored for Leadership and Scholarly Contributions as 2026 ASHE Fellow
Dr. Jeni Hart has been named a 2026 Fellow by the Association for the Study of Higher Education (ASHE), a national organization that serves the public good. Dr. Hart serves as Dean of the Graduate School, Vice Provost for Graduate Studies, and Professor of Higher Education in the Department of Educational Leadership and Policy Analysis in the College of Education and Human Development. She researches faculty work and the organizational structures that shape campus climate. Part-Time Job Resources for Grad Students
Finding a part-time job while pursuing your graduate studies can be a great way to gain valuable experience, earn extra income, and connect with the campus community. Here are some tips to help you get started. September 3: Part-Time Campus Job Fair This Thursday, September 4, head over to Lowry Mall 10 a.m.-1 p.m. for the Part-Time Campus Job Fair. This is a fantastic opportunity to meet on- and off-campus employers in person. Remember to bring your student ID, copies of your resume, and your class schedule.
